bullets: Designed and built the camera-processing service at the core of NEXA, a real-time video-analytics platform: one process per camera, with a plug-in framework that now hosts 20+ detection pipelines built by me and 6 other engineers.
Built the shared GPU model-serving layer (up to 16 stateless model workers) and the alerting path, then moved alerts from Kafka to Redis Streams with no lost alerts.
On a lab server, raised cameras per server 4× (~4 → 16) by moving 12 models to NVIDIA Triton + TensorRT and decoding video on the GPU. Production rollout planned.
Set hardware sizing limits by load-testing each machine to failure: 10 cameras per cloud T4 server and 8 per NVIDIA Jetson edge device.
Built an MLflow model registry with roles, promotion and rollback, and checksum-verified model delivery; now training a junior engineer to take it into production.
Found and fixed a 31-hour silent outage, and shipped release v1.1.0 to all three production servers with zero data loss.
